newsitem.title: USA: ConEd says record power demand likely Tues.
newsitem.headline: ConEd says record power demand likely Tues.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd) said continued heat and humidity could push power demand on its system to a record high Tuesday.
"There's a very good possibility we could break our record today," said ConEd spokesman Richard Mulieri.
The standing record load on ConEd's system is 10,805 megawatts (MW), set August 2, 1995.
Mulieri said the company expected to see demand from its 2.9 million customers peak around 1600-1700 EDT, when air conditioners are putting the heaviest strain of the day on the system.
Meteorologists are predicting the temperature in Central Park will hit a sweltering 96 degrees Fahrenheit Tuesday, following a reading of 94 F Monday.
Mulieri said the power grid was holding up well with the exception of the Granite Hill substation in Westchester County, just north of New York City, which shut down last night.
The substation carries about 240 MW of load to the northern Yonkers area. The cause of the outage was not yet known, Mulieri said.

He said there were no problems on ConEd's high-voltage transmission lines, and that the utility still has access to generation reserves about 18 percent above actual demand, the cushion members of the New York Power Pool are required to maintain in order to handle emergencies.
